headline: The suite's hardest CSS compiles away on every build-time lane, but `styled(TabInternal)` denies `@yak/solid` the fold and costs it 12.9 of its 16.0 ms per render in Solid's component machinery.

microbench.why: `vanilla-solid` at 192,000 renders/s leads, with `next-yak-css` at 160,000 and `vanilla` at 156,000. `next-yak` at 82,500 keeps one wrapper per tab, which the css prop avoids by compiling to a plain class. `yak-solid` at 11,100 is the case's outlier: `Tab` is `styled(TabInternal)`, so folding never applies, and 12.9 of its 16.0 ms per render sits in `@solidjs/signals` and `@solidjs/web` building a component and a reactive scope for every tab. `cnfast` at 72,200 and `cn` at 71,300 resolve a ~40-token list per tab from cache.

autocannon.why: `vanilla-solid` at 752 req/s and `vanilla` at 721 lead, `next-yak-css` at 684 close behind. `yak-solid` at 72 req/s is last, since the per-tab component instantiation runs inside every request.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

attribution.why: `vanilla-solid` at 1.13 ms leads, then `stylex` at 1.34 ms and `next-yak-css` at 1.43 ms, all with an empty lib bucket — the css prop compiles to a class, StyleX resolved at build time, and the hand-written lane never had a library. `next-yak` at 3.08 ms books 0.739 ms of lib for its per-tab wrapper. `emotion` at 22.2 ms books 16.9 ms of its own: the full state matrix, serialized per tab.

hydrate.why: `vanilla-solid` at 41.8 ms leads and `next-yak-css` at 47.3 ms heads a tight React field. `yak-solid` at 118 ms walks the same unfolded wrappers it built on the server, and `goober` at 195 ms and `styled-components` at 193 ms inject a large sheet while attaching.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

inp.why: `cn` at 6.6 ms and `stylex` at 6.6 ms lead, and most lanes answer between 7 and 9 ms. The Solid lanes read 18.5 ms and 79.2 ms because their signal bump changes the group's tab count, so the list is rebuilt rather than left alone — the React pass re-renders the same tabs and writes nothing. `emotion` at 27.6 ms and `panda-props` at 25.6 ms are slow on mechanism.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

mount.why: `vanilla-solid` mounts in 29.5 ms against 92.7 ms for `vanilla` — Solid builds this DOM from cloned templates while React constructs a fiber tree for 16 elements per group. `yak-solid` at 99.6 ms gives that advantage back to the per-tab component instantiation. `emotion` at 224 ms and `styled-components` at 201 ms inject before the first paint.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane at roughly 0.87 ms, the highest in the suite: the anchor-positioned underline and the `@supports` fallbacks make the match expensive, and every lane pays it equally.

payload.why: `vanilla` at 2,690 gz B and the next-yak css-prop lanes at roughly 2,700 B are the floor. `yak-solid` reaches 8,303 B with 3,936 B of HTML — 16 elements per group, each carrying a hydration key. The utility lanes are the heavy end at 21.1–23.5 kB, `cn` highest, since a ~40-token class list per tab lands in both the markup and the merge runtime.

nsweep.why: `vanilla-solid` holds 24.9 ms at the largest size with `vanilla` at 29.4 ms; `next-yak` reaches 65.7 ms for its per-tab wrapper. `yak-solid` at 503 ms has the steepest line in the suite, one component instantiation per tab all the way up.

crossCase: Paired with the Example `multifile-composition`, which is this exact workload with the primitives moved to an imported module. `next-yak` moves 82,500 to 81,000 renders/s and `yak-solid` 11,100 to 10,000, so the module boundary costs both of them little here — the fold was already lost to `styled(TabInternal)` inside a single file. What defeats folding in this component is the component target, not the file layout.
